title: Operational Group Assessment / LAST CALL
summary: Operational and behavioural assessment of the independent group known as Last Call.
body:
SUBJECT

LAST CALL

Current designation for a small independent group operating primarily within Free-Void territory.

The group was separated and detained following an incident in late August, 323 SE. Members were subsequently imprisoned at separate facilities and remained in custody until late November, 333 SE.

No formal organisation, corporate registration, House affiliation or recognised military command structure has been identified. The group nevertheless demonstrates a degree of internal cohesion inconsistent with its apparent history.

SOURCE LIMITATIONS

This record is assembled from surveillance, recovered documentation, institutional records, intercepted communications and indirect reporting.

Ishida, Lorenzo is considered an indirect source only. He is not affiliated with Brightside and is not believed to be aware of Brightside observation. Information attributed to Ishida has been retained where independently corroborated.

INDIVIDUAL ASSESSMENTS

KENJI

Origin: Monument. City of Luoyang.

Kenji is an orphan originating from Luoyang. He was taken in by Saigyou Norisuke and subsequently trained in security work. Available assessments indicate an innate level of combat aptitude beyond what his formal training would reasonably account for.

Outside violent encounters, Kenji presents as an ordinary individual and does not display a consistent desire for violence. During active conflict this changes considerably.

Kenji appears to possess an unusually low threshold for deciding that a confrontation should end permanently. Once committed to violence, he acts rapidly and with little apparent hesitation. Encounters involving Kenji have a disproportionately high likelihood of ending in death.

Assessment: Kenji is not believed to seek violence. He is, however, exceptionally willing to conclude it.

KALLISTA

Origin: Globe II, designation Terath.

Kallista is not believed to be native to this world. References to her origin appear in Vulcan Research Authority documentation.

Kallista is frequently quiet and can appear apathetic to circumstances that would normally produce a stronger emotional response. This should not be interpreted as a lack of awareness.

She demonstrates a strong sensitivity to language. She notices specific wording, omissions and changes in phrasing that other members of the group frequently overlook.

The extent of her knowledge regarding Globe II and Terath remains unknown.

Assessment: Kallista's apparent passivity should not be mistaken for inattentiveness. She listens more closely than she speaks.

RUBY

Surname: Unknown.
Origin: Probable Stwyx.
Current identity: Equin citizen, presumed constructed.

Ruby's documented identity is believed to be false. Available evidence suggests an origin on Stwyx, an analogue world not intended for ordinary travel or civilian departure. Her present Equin identity is assessed as fabricated or substantially altered.

Ruby possesses advanced academic qualifications in engineering, computer science and propulsion science, with exceptionally high marks.

The disparity between demonstrated technical ability and personal self-assessment is considerable. Ruby routinely underestimates her own competence and is unusually receptive to criticism from individuals she perceives as more capable or authoritative.

A previous dependency on stimulants is documented. Current use appears limited, but the history remains operationally relevant. Pressure, stress and controlled access to resources may represent effective leverage.

Assessment: Ruby is considerably more capable than she believes herself to be. This discrepancy is exploitable.

ZEPHYR

Model classification: Legacy clanker.
Probable manufacturer: Lexxir Guild.

Zephyr was initially assessed as an unremarkable legacy artificial individual. Earlier records contain little of operational interest.

This assessment changed following the discovery of an internal Lexxir department responsible for his model line. The department and its purpose remain under investigation.

Zephyr demonstrates a strong and unusually consistent concept of moral justice. He appears to retain an attachment to the period in which artificial sapience was more broadly recognised. The loss of that social position may have altered his understanding of personhood, authority and obligation in ways that remain poorly understood.

Zephyr is extremely dangerous in direct conflict. His violence is deliberate rather than uncontrolled.

A particular behavioural priority has been repeatedly observed: Zephyr will defend Ruby against perceived threats, insults or coercion. The intensity of this response appears disproportionate to the immediate threat.

Assessment: Zephyr should not be treated as a passive machine or obsolete security platform. Current behaviour suggests an individual with a developed moral framework and unresolved historical grievance.

LUCY MAYER

Original designation: LY-7-7.
Programme: Lyrix.
Origin: Apex.

Lucy Mayer was originally designated LY-7-7 and produced as part of the Lyrix programme on Apex. The programme involved genetically modified human subjects intended for piloting through the Echo and for specialised military and black-operations deployment.

Lucy was not exposed to ordinary civilian life during her early development. Records indicate that she was approximately fourteen years old when she was removed from an Apex site during an attack by an individual identified as Conner Mayer. She subsequently became Lucy Mayer.

Lucy displays significant emotional immaturity in some circumstances. She is highly curious and demonstrates a persistent interest in experiences outside the narrow environment in which she was raised.

She is also somewhat dependent on low-tier stimulants. The behaviour appears partly recreational and partly functional.

The combination of military conditioning, restricted childhood development and sudden exposure to ordinary society produces behaviour that is difficult to classify using conventional models.

Assessment: Lucy's curiosity should not be mistaken for naivety. She has been trained to operate in environments where hesitation is dangerous. Her difficulty lies elsewhere: she is still learning what ordinary people consider worth hesitating over.

GROUP PSYCHOLOGY

The group does not appear to possess a permanent leader. Authority is situational. Individual members assume control according to circumstance, after which the others generally accept the decision without prolonged dispute.

Disagreements are usually short. Group cohesion appears to increase when circumstances deteriorate.

INFORMATION ANOMALIES

Several observations contained in this record cannot be satisfactorily attributed to a known source.

1. Members have demonstrated awareness of information discussed in locations where no confirmed member of Last Call was present.

2. The group has altered course shortly before information became available that would have justified the alteration.

3. Individual members have demonstrated knowledge of technical, geographical and institutional details not present in their known education or employment history.

4. Behavioural predictions made before the 323 SE separation remained accurate after the group's ten-year imprisonment and separation interval.

The fourth observation requires additional review.

INTERNAL NOTE

They know when something is wrong before they know what is wrong.

Source unknown.
